newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Port of Rotterdam turnover falls 0.9 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Port of Rotterdam turnover falls 0.9 pct in 1996.

text.p: Port of Rotterdam turnover in 1996 fell 0.9 percent to 290.6 million tonnes from 1995's record 294.3 million tonnes, the port said on Tuesday.

It said a principle reason for the decline was the fall in imports of iron ore and scrap. Throughput of iron ore to Germany was down seven million tonnes from 1995 to 16.4 million with reduced consumption of steel and rising ore stocks in Germany.
Economic slowdown across Europe had a negative impact on the results as it had on all European ports, although Rotterdam's share in the Hamburg/Le Havre range held at 42 percent.
Growth of container shipping was also more muted than in the last five years, rising only 0.5 percent to 3.9 million containers.
Rotterdam has suffered as Britain has increasingly shipped containers directly to and from other continents rather than via Rotterdam. Channel Tunnel trade has also taken its toll.
However, two areas of promise in 1996 were crude oil and coal.
Crude oil traffic reached a peak of 99.8 million tonnes, although shipments tailed off in the second half of the year.
Coal shipments also rose by 9.0 percent to 19.5 million tonnes.
Overall prospects for 1997 were brighter with an expected improvement in the German economy.
Growth of container shipping is also expected to be better than previously thought. In the year 2010, the Rotterdam Port Management believes container traffic to amount to 7.5 million units.
Investment this year amounted to a hefty eight billion guilders, but the port said growth was dependent upon the support of the Dutch government.
Port Alderman, Herman van den Muijsenberg, used his annual review to urge the government to reach a swift decision on possible port expansion into the North Sea.
"The expansion of the port and its industrial sites is becoming increasingly urgent," he said.
The government must reach a decision next year.
